Figure III-1 traces the projected baseline non-Crow and Crow employment associated with moderate development. It also shows the changes in employment attributable to Westmoreland's activity. In other words, these differences could be attributed to the entrance of Westmoreland, after allowing for labor requirements of other coal development. Figure III-1 employment includes basic as well as non-basic employment. Tables 1-3 in Appendix I show the split between the two employment types.
Westmoreland Resources high level of development (26 MTPY), (Scenario 2) is also traced in Figure III-1. Employment levels and trends are quite similar to those for the low level until 1990, after which employment levels for high development exceed that for lower development. Figure III-1 also shows the results from construction of an energy conversion facility particularly the very high employment levels. Of particular interest are the extreme temporary employment peaks during the construction period. By 1984, production employment would replace construction employment. Employment reaches its maximum level in 1986.
Figure III-2 traces the baseline employment projections for both levels of projected Crow coal development. In the lower set of trend lines the baseline assumes no other coal mining of the Crow coal reserves and compares this with the most probable level of Westmoreland development. Figure III-2 also shows the impact of Westmoreland's most probable level of development during periods when other significant Crow coal development is taking place simultaneously.
